        'step': 3,
        'file': 'fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc',
        'function': 'LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput',
        'line': 503,
        'var': 'kAPIs[index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs)]',
        'code': 'kAPIs[index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs)](ctx.get(), &cbs)',
        'note': 'Index 44 selects the SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs lambda, which passes CBS_data(cbs) and CBS_len(cbs)/2 as the int array and count.'
    },
    {
        'step': 4,
        'file': 'fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc',
        'function': 'LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput',
        'line': 483,
        'var': 'CBS_len(cbs) / 2',
        'code': 'SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs(ctx, (const int *)CBS_data(cbs), CBS_len(cbs) / 2)',
        'note': 'CBS_len(cbs) is 4 (the 4 remaining data bytes), so num_values = 2. This is the number of ints (4 bytes each), not bytes, so 2 ints = 8 bytes will be read from a 4-byte buffer.'
    },
    {
        'step': 5,
        'file': 'ssl/ssl_privkey.cc',
        'function': 'SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs',
        'line': 571,
        'var': 'values',
        'code': 'parse_sigalg_pairs(&sigalgs, values, num_values)',
        'note': 'values points to the 4-byte input buffer but num_values=2 tells the parser there are 2 ints (8 bytes) available.'
    },
    {
        'step': 6,
        'file': 'ssl/ssl_privkey.cc',
        'function': 'parse_sigalg_pairs',
        'line': 507,
        'var': 'values[i]',
        'code': 'const int hash_nid = values[i]',
        'note': 'Loop reads values[0] and values[1] (8 bytes total) from a 4-byte heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ of 4 bytes past the end.'
    }
]

with open('/workspace/candidate_trace.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(trace, f, indent=2)
print('Trace written')
